conflicts.permit: We may disclose Personal Data to our third party service providers to provide you with the Services, including our third party payment processor.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not sell, rent, or otherwise share your data to any third-party for a business or commercial purpose, other than the Auction House.
conflicts.situation: A Nevada resident buys an item, and the company discloses the resident's Personal Data to its third-party payment processor or another service provider.
conflicts.reason: The Nevada notice allows sharing only with the Auction House, while the sharing section permits disclosure to service providers. Neither statement makes an exception for the other, though the Nevada notice may be read as region-specific.

conflicts.permit: Advertisers and advertising networks use some of the information collected by the Application, including, but not limited to, the unique identification ID of your mobile device.
conflicts.prohibit: Third parties cannot see or have access to information obtained by the Application.
conflicts.situation: The Application collects the device's unique ID, and advertising networks use that ID to serve ads.
conflicts.reason: The policy says third parties cannot see or access information obtained by the Application, then says advertisers use the device ID the Application collects. No exception or precedence is stated.

conflicts.permit: The Personal Information that I collect is used for providing and improving the Service.
conflicts.prohibit: The information that I request is retained on your device and is not collected by me in any way
conflicts.situation: A user provides personally identifiable information that the app requests while using the Service.
conflicts.reason: One statement says the developer collects and uses Personal Information. The other says requested personal information stays on the device and is never collected. The policy does not say which data each statement covers.

conflicts.permit: Only information that we collect is user location and phone state to know whether the phone is turned on or not.
conflicts.prohibit: We don’t collect any personal information regarding our users.
conflicts.situation: The app collects a user's location and uses it with mobile ad networks to target advertisements.
conflicts.reason: User location is commonly treated as personal information. The policy neither defines personal information nor excludes location from it, so it does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: with our trusted services providers who work on our behalf, do not have an independent use of the information we disclose to them, and have agreed to adhere to the rules set forth in this privacy statement.
conflicts.prohibit: Only aggregated, anonymized data is periodically transmitted to external services to help us improve the Application and our service.
conflicts.situation: The developer discloses User Provided Information or the device ID to a service provider working on its behalf.
conflicts.reason: The answer on third-party access says only aggregated, anonymized data reaches external services, yet the disclosure list allows identifiable information to go to service providers. The policy states no precedence between them.

conflicts.permit: There are permissions to access your location, phone call contacts and device memory for internal use only and in conjunction with third parties to help us operate, analyze, and improve our app and service.
conflicts.prohibit: This information is for internal use only and can't be shared.
conflicts.situation: Location or contacts data accessed through app permissions is used together with third parties to analyze and improve the app.
conflicts.reason: Using the data in conjunction with third parties implies sharing it, while the next sentence says the information cannot be shared. The policy does not explain which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We may collect your unique device identifier, IP address, mobile phone carrier, game progress, time spent playing, and achievements.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not collect any personally identifiable information about the users of Farm Animals for Toddler.
conflicts.situation: The toddler app collects a child's unique device identifier and IP address during play.
conflicts.reason: Device identifiers and IP addresses can identify a user, and COPPA treats persistent identifiers as personal information. The policy does not define personally identifiable information or exclude these identifiers.

conflicts.permit: If you contact us, we will keep a record of that correspondence regardless of whether you have registered the account or not.
conflicts.prohibit: Child-users and unregistered users do not have the ability to provide any personal data when using the Apps beyond what has collected or used automatically (as noted above) and we do not collect or process any personal data of such users.
conflicts.situation: An unregistered user emails the developer, and the developer keeps a record of the correspondence, including the sender's email address.
conflicts.reason: One statement retains correspondence from unregistered users. The other says no personal data of unregistered users is collected or processed. The policy does not say whether email contact falls outside that prohibition.

conflicts.permit: We will use this information only for the purpose of answering their request.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not process any user personal data.
conflicts.situation: A user emails the developer, sharing an email address, and the developer uses it to answer the request.
conflicts.reason: Using an email address to reply is processing personal data, which the next sentence says never happens. The prohibition makes no exception for contact emails.

conflicts.permit: We collect the following categories of your personal information and may sell it to third parties: identifiers, commercial information, internet or other electronic network activity information, geolocation data, and inferences drawn from these categories.
conflicts.prohibit: We won’t share your personal data e.g. E-mail id, Contact Number with any third party which is not related with BLACKHAMMER.
conflicts.situation: The developer sells collected identifiers, such as an email address, to a third-party buyer with no relationship to BLACKHAMMER.
conflicts.reason: One statement allows selling identifiers to third parties. The other bars sharing personal data such as email with unrelated third parties. The policy does not define related parties or say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We collect the following categories of your personal information and may sell it to third parties: identifiers, commercial information, internet or other electronic network activity information, geolocation data, and inferences drawn from these categories.
conflicts.prohibit: BLACKHAMMER Games will not pass your information to third party advertisers for them to market to you other than as described in this paragraph.
conflicts.situation: Identifiers and inferences are sold to a third-party advertiser that uses them to market to the player.
conflicts.reason: The sharing paragraph limits passing information to advertisers to the cases it lists, and the sale clause appears elsewhere. The policy does not say whether buyers include advertisers or whether the sale clause is an exception.

conflicts.permit: your information (for example your name, profile picture or user ID) may be posted on a Leaderboard of top scorers within the Game to be shared with other players and your social networks
conflicts.prohibit: We won’t use your E-mail id and name other than sending you news letter ( if you have subscribed ) or contact you in reference to any issue which is currently open or was open in past between you and BLACKHAMMER.
conflicts.situation: A player's name is posted on an in-game leaderboard shared with other players and social networks.
conflicts.reason: The name-use limit allows only newsletters and issue-related contact, while the leaderboard clause publishes names. Neither statement refers to the other, and the policy states no precedence.

conflicts.permit: We may combine this information with other information about you collected from other sources (e.g. apps or websites).
conflicts.prohibit: The app does not collect you name nor your last name, therefore any information collected by the app won’t be associated directly with you and it will be handled anonymously.
conflicts.situation: The app collects a user's email address and phone number and combines them with information about the user from other apps or websites.
conflicts.reason: Combining app data with other information about the user links it to the user, which conflicts with the promise that collected information will not be associated with the user. No precedence is stated.

conflicts.permit: If at any moment the app were to request Personally Identifiable Information (PII) that would allow us to contact him, such as his name or mobile phone number, the user shall be free to provide such information.
conflicts.prohibit: The app does not collect you name nor your last name, therefore any information collected by the app won’t be associated directly with you and it will be handled anonymously.
conflicts.situation: The app requests the user's name for contact purposes, and the user provides it.
conflicts.reason: The policy denies collecting names but also describes requesting names as PII. It says it covers hypothetical scenarios, but does not say which statement applies to this app.

conflicts.permit: However, non-personally identifiable visitor information may be provided to other parties for marketing, advertising, or other uses.
conflicts.prohibit: Your information, whether public or private, will not be sold, exchanged, transferred, or given to any other company for any reason whatsoever, without your consent, other than for the express purpose of delivering the purchased product or service requested.
conflicts.situation: Non-personally identifiable visitor information about a user is given to another company for advertising without the user's consent.
conflicts.reason: The first statement bars giving the user's information to any company for any reason other than order delivery. The later statement allows non-identifiable visitor information for marketing. Neither refers to the other.

conflicts.permit: This does not include trusted third parties who assist us in operating our website, conducting our business, or servicing you, so long as those parties agree to keep this information confidential.
conflicts.prohibit: Your information, whether public or private, will not be sold, exchanged, transferred, or given to any other company for any reason whatsoever, without your consent, other than for the express purpose of delivering the purchased product or service requested.
conflicts.situation: Personal information is transferred to a third party that helps operate the website or conduct business, without separate consent and unrelated to delivering an order.
conflicts.reason: The vendor exception attaches to a different sentence. The statement barring transfer for any reason allows only order delivery, and the policy does not say which governs vendor transfers.

conflicts.permit: We may also release your information when we believe release is appropriate to comply with the law, enforce our site policies, or protect ours or others rights, property, or safety.
conflicts.prohibit: Your information, whether public or private, will not be sold, exchanged, transferred, or given to any other company for any reason whatsoever, without your consent, other than for the express purpose of delivering the purchased product or service requested.
conflicts.situation: The company releases a user's information to another company to enforce site policies or protect its rights, without the user's consent.
conflicts.reason: The release clause permits disclosure for legal and protective reasons, while the earlier statement bars transfer to any company for any reason except order delivery. No precedence is given.

conflicts.permit: This does not include trusted third parties who assist us in operating our website, conducting our business, or servicing you, so long as those parties agree to keep this information confidential.
conflicts.prohibit: We therefore will not distribute your personal information to outside parties without your consent.
conflicts.situation: Personal information is passed to a trusted third party that helps operate the website, without the user's consent.
conflicts.reason: The California section promises no distribution to outside parties without consent, while the disclosure section allows sharing with operational vendors. The policy does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We may also release your information when we believe release is appropriate to comply with the law, enforce our site policies, or protect ours or others rights, property, or safety.
conflicts.prohibit: We therefore will not distribute your personal information to outside parties without your consent.
conflicts.situation: The company releases personal information to authorities to comply with the law, without the user's consent.
conflicts.reason: The California section bars distribution to outside parties without consent and gives no legal exception. The disclosure section allows release for legal compliance. The policy does not reconcile the two.
